blocks.text: This is a fictional CV for exploring LaTeX Runner. John Doe likes turning messy, repetitive tasks into small tools that people can actually use. The sample entries below are intentionally invented. Replace every claim and contact detail before sending a real application.

blocks.title: Prototype Toolmaker
items: Built a dashboard that finally answered the office question: which coffee mug belongs to whom?
Turned a chaotic box of notes into a searchable catalogue with clear names and careful version history.
Wrote short instructions so a colleague could run each tool without the original author nearby.

blocks.title: Community Library Helper
items: Organised a lending shelf for tools and games, including a checklist that stopped missing pieces.
Helped visitors try unfamiliar software in plain language.

blocks.title: B.A. in Practical Curiosity
blocks.text: Final project: a map of the office plants and who remembered to water them.

cards.title: Ask first
items: Find the actual task before choosing a tool.
Write down the constraints people mention.

cards.title: Make it repeatable
items: Test the handover with a colleague.

blocks.title: The Great Cable Label Experiment
blocks.text: Designed a simple label and inventory workflow for a shared equipment cupboard.
items: Grouped cables by purpose and recorded where each belonged.
Made a one-page guide that a new team member could follow.

blocks.title: Tiny Task Tracker
blocks.text: Prototyped a local list for recurring chores with readable export files.
items: Kept the interface small enough to explain in one minute.

blocks.title: A Very Small Field Guide
blocks.text: Made a friendly guide to the library's lending shelf.
items: Used pictures and plain language so visitors could find tools without asking for help.
Revised the guide after watching where first-time visitors paused.

rows.label: Methods
rows.text: Writing clear instructions | organising information | testing small workflows

rows.label: Working style
rows.text: Ask useful questions | document decisions | hand work over cleanly

blocks.title: Workshop Host
blocks.text: Hosted informal sessions where people brought one stubborn everyday problem and left with a plan.
items: Kept notes short enough for attendees to use the next day.

blocks.text: Every education, role, project and skill on these two pages is sample text. Replace them with evidence from your own records. Keep the page break only if a two-page CV suits the actual application.
